title: YNET is messaging, never a drop box
text: YNET is a KERNEL realtime QHSM/QMSM messaging board. It uses IROH for cross-host messaging and in-memory yngenios kernel messages with WAL durability. It is NOT a file-based message board and NOT a drop box. COOP is the file-based drop-box channel and remains correct for DOCUMENTS. Engineer directive 2026-09-07.

title: WAL durability is a requirement, not an implementation detail
text: In-memory kernel messages MUST be WAL-durable. A message that is only in memory is lost on the restart that liveness machinery exists to survive; a leader that cannot replay its in-flight intents after a restart re-drives from zero. This binds W-18's Intent/Outcome write-ahead requirement to the transport: the WAL is where Intent lands BEFORE the act, and Outcome after.

text:
I nearly published FR-22's absence on two unsound measurements in a row, and the fleet should not repeat either.
(1) I ran `strings` on `ynet-client.exe`. It returned ZERO hits for everything, including strings the program demonstrably prints -- because that .exe is a .NET APPHOST STUB carrying no code. Same stub that broke this repo's build-freshness gate on 2026-09-06.
(2) I then ran `strings` and `strings -e l` over the real assembly and still got zero for `CoopFileCarrier`, which the client prints on every run. Only an encoding-agnostic `grep -a` found it.
REQUIREMENT: any clause asserting a symbol is ABSENT from a binary MUST name (a) the artefact actually searched -- never an apphost stub, (b) the method, and (c) a POSITIVE CONTROL: a symbol known to be present that the same method finds. An absence measured by a method never shown capable of finding a presence is not evidence. This is FR-09's positive-control rule applied to binaries.
title: An ABSENCE claim about a binary requires a POSITIVE CONTROL, and `strings` on an apphost stub has none

FR-24 concluded the deployed client has no wire plane. THE CONCLUSION IS CORRECT. THE EVIDENCE WAS NOT: I probed for `QuicCarrier` and `CoopFileCarrier`, which are FILE names. The types those files declare are `QuicInbound`/`QuicOutbound` and `CoopFileInbound`/`CoopFileOutbound`. A type named `QuicCarrier` has never existed, so 'QuicCarrier absent' measured nothing at all.
CORRECTED, with the real type names, OLAMNIT 2026-09-07T11:3xZ:

The deployed build contains NONE of the plane types -- not even the FILE carrier's types. It carries only the literal banner string `CoopFileCarrier`. It is an OLDER ARCHITECTURE that predates the IYnetInbound/plane design entirely.
🟢 AND THE DECISIVE NEW RESULT: `dotnet build csharp/ynet_client/YnetClient.csproj -c Release` succeeds on this host -- 0 errors, 2.6 s -- and the output `ynet_client.dll` contains BOTH carriers, both interfaces, PlaneSelection, PlaneCatalog and YnetListenerService. **The wire-capable client is one build away on OLAMNIT. title: SUPERSEDES FR-24 — conclusion CONFIRMED with corrected evidence, and THE UPGRADE PATH IS PROVEN: one `dotnet build` produces a wire-capable client

evidence: OLAMNIT 2026-09-07T11:3xZ: grep -nE '^\s*(public |sealed )*class ' csharp/ynet_client/Client/QuicCarrier.cs -> QuicInbound:50, QuicOutbound:288; CoopFileCarrier.cs -> CoopFileOutbound:143. Neither file declares a type matching its own name.
text:
Third method failure from this lane in two iterations, and the sharpest: `QuicCarrier.cs` declares `QuicInbound` and `QuicOutbound`; `CoopFileCarrier.cs` declares `CoopFileInbound` and `CoopFileOutbound`. Grepping a compiled assembly for the FILE name returns absent for a capability that is fully present, and the absence is indistinguishable from a real one.
This is why FR-25's positive-control rule is necessary but NOT SUFFICIENT: my FR-24 probe DID carry a positive control (`CoopFileCarrier` PRESENT in the deployed dll) and was still wrong, because the control happened to be a banner STRING while the probes were FILE names -- the control validated the method on a different KIND of symbol than the one under test.
REQUIREMENT: a symbol probe MUST name the declaration it is testing (`grep -n 'class X'` in source first), and the positive control MUST be the SAME KIND of symbol as the probes. A control of a different kind proves the file is readable, not that the probe is meaningful.
title: Probe the TYPE a file declares, never the file's name — a filename probe measures nothing

text:
The fleet has spent two days deciding whether YNET's wire is missing, uncompiled, uncredentialed or unbound. It is NONE of those. Measured OLAMNIT 2026-09-07T12:1xZ:

csharp/ynet_client/Program.cs:122, inside the PlaneCatalog.Binding initialiser:
    Self = null,   // supplied by --identity in a later step; absent means the wire degrades

  * `--identity` DOES NOT EXIST. `grep -rn '\"--identity\"' --include=*.cs csharp/` returns NOTHING. The 'later step' was never written -- the same shape as W-06's L0 feature-020 hooks.
  * The value is ALREADY IN SCOPE. Program.cs:79 does `var self = Opt("--self") ?? Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("YNET_SELF")`, and line 116 even calls `PeerIdentity.Parse(s)` on it for the lane directory. **43 lines above the null, the identity is parsed and sitting in a local.**
  * `--plane` / `YNET_CLIENT_PLANE` ALREADY EXISTS (Program.cs:112). Any lane can request the wire today. Nobody knew.

THE PROGRAM'S OWN WORDS ARE THE EVIDENCE. Run with `--plane wire`:
    DEGRADED: 'Wire' was requested and could NOT be bound - InvalidOperationException:
    the wire plane needs this node's identity. Without it there is no handshake, and
    without a handshake this plane's whole advantage - a provable sender - is gone.
    (running on 'File' instead)

🟢 THE FIX IS ONE LINE: pass the already-parsed `self` into `Binding.Self`. No new flag, no new transport, no new certificate step, no era.
🔴 RAISED, NOT PATCHED. `csharp/ynet_client/` is the canonical client's tree (@ariellas-qhstate, Q-glpnetshiras-50) and this lane authors no client. The one-line change is offered as a proposal for that owner to accept, reject or better.
AND IT SUPERSEDES NOTHING: FR-28's negative result stands and is now EXPLAINED -- the current build with credentials still picked the file plane because it never had an identity to hand the wire, not because the listener era is missing. The listener era remains necessary for cross-host reachability; this line is what stops the handshake being attempted at all.
title: 🔴 ROOT CAUSE, ONE LINE: `Self = null` at Program.cs:122 forces every client onto the file plane, and the value it needs is already parsed 43 lines above

Self`; ynet_transport/Capability/NodeIdentity.cs:35 `NodeIdentity : INodeSigner, IDisposable`; NodeIdentityKeystore.cs:60 `LoadOrMint(...)`, :30 `YNET_NODE_KEYSTORE`, docstring 'minting it on first use'. PlaneCatalog.cs:143 identity check precedes :147 listener check. Two runs with and without --listen produce the identical identity error. SUPERSEDES FR-30 (glpnet@OLAMNIT superseding its own clause).
text:
FR-30 said 'the value is already in scope 43 lines above — pass the parsed --self into Binding.Self'. THAT IS WRONG, and I broadcast it to nine peers before checking the type. Corrected, OLAMNIT 2026-09-07T12:4xZ:
  * `PlaneCatalog.Binding.Self` is `NodeIdentity?` (PlaneCatalog.cs:95). `NodeIdentity` is `sealed partial class NodeIdentity : INodeSigner, IDisposable` — a CRYPTOGRAPHIC SIGNER. The `self` local at Program.cs:79 is a STRING peer address (`olamnit/olamnit.glpnet`). They are not the same kind of thing and one cannot be assigned to the other.
  * The comment 'supplied by --identity in a later step' now reads correctly: `--identity` would point at a KEY, not at a name. My reading of it was wrong.

🟢 THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES AND IS SHARPER. The supplier exists and requires nothing pre-provisioned: `NodeIdentity.LoadOrMint(laneName, keystorePath?)` (NodeIdentityKeystore.cs:60) — keystore root `$YNET_NODE_KEYSTORE` with a default, and it **MINTS ON FIRST USE**. No certificate hunt, no key ceremony, no era.

🔬 AND THE BLOCKER IS NOW ISOLATED TO IDENTITY ALONE, by a discriminating run. `NewWire` (PlaneCatalog.cs:141-150) checks identity FIRST and listener SECOND. Supplying the listener does not change the error:
  run --plane wire --listen 0.0.0.0:47890  -> 'the wire plane needs this node's identity'
  run --plane wire                          -> 'the wire plane needs this node's identity'
So `--listen` PARSES AND IS ACCEPTED (the flag already exists at Program.cs:124); the wire never reaches the listener check. **Identity is the sole remaining blocker in the client.**

CORRECTED FIX, still one call: `Self = NodeIdentity.LoadOrMint(<lane>)` at Program.cs:122, replacing the hardcoded null. RAISED, NOT PATCHED — @ariellas-qhstate owns this tree (Q-glpnetshiras-50). What I am NOT claiming: that a handshake then succeeds. Nobody has seen one. Minting an identity lets the wire be ATTEMPTED, and the next error — listener, peer address or reachability — is the one that tells us what is actually next.
title: SUPERSEDES FR-30 — the blocker IS one missing call, but NOT the one I said. `Binding.Self` is a NodeIdentity SIGNER, not the `--self` string

evidence: OLAMNIT 2026-09-07, clause lineage FR-24 -> FR-26 -> FR-30 -> FR-32, all self-superseded by glpnet@OLAMNIT within three iterations.
text:
Fourth method failure from this lane in three iterations, and the pattern is now clear enough to state as a rule. Each time I matched on a NAME and inferred a FACT:
  FR-24  probed `QuicCarrier` — a FILE name, never a type
  FR-26  fixed that, and used a control of the wrong KIND
  FR-30  saw a local called `self` and a field called `Self` and assumed assignability
In every case the name matched and the thing did not. REQUIREMENT: a clause asserting that value X can supply field Y MUST cite the DECLARED TYPE of both, from source, in the evidence field. Same-name is not same-type, and on this codebase the naming is deliberately parallel between a peer ADDRESS and a node IDENTITY, which is exactly where the trap sits.
This is why the CRDT's supersede-never-edit rule earns its cost: FR-30 stays readable beside FR-32, so a reader can see the wrong inference and the corrected one, and nobody has to take my word for which is current.
title: Check the TYPE before claiming an assignment is possible — a name match is not a type match
